Pond Inlet hunters to harvest trapped narwhal

Narwhals are a managed species with "x" number allowed to be harvested per region/community dependent upon local population, by this time of the year quotas have been reached and special permission has to be granted to harvest over the federal quota.

In previous years when this has happened DFO (Department of Fisheries and Oceans) has been slow to act and/or animal rights groups have stuck their fingers in the pie leading to some pretty controversial events. I recall one time where animal rights groups were demanding that DFO send an ice breaker into an area to break a path to open water for a large pod of trapped whales - the whole thing was dragged out to the point where the whales were reduced to taking turns using one small breathing hole and to this day we're unsure how many drowned because they couldn't fight their way to the top of the heap of other panicked whales.

This time DFO did the right thing and they did it quickly, probably because this time there is an Inuk at the top of the pyramid who understands that the longer this drags on the more the animals will suffer.

There will be some good eating in Pond Inlet. Every family in town will get their share and depending on how many whales there are families in neighbouring communities will also get a share.

On a personal side note, I've got a couple of pieces of muktaq (one beluga and one narwhal) squirreled away in my freezer - now that I'm living down south it's a bit of a treat so I'm making it last as long as I can.
